name: Sasa Ferrari
evidence: A well-documented prospect who already uses hiring analytics
detail: Ironclad has published information about Sasa’s role, its growth and its interview process. It also describes her team reviewing recruiting metrics in Ashby.
demonstrates: Show a grounded first draft that acknowledges the team’s existing tools instead of assuming they lack visibility into hiring.

name: Adam Ward
evidence: Cursor in one source, SpaceXAI in another
detail: Adam’s profile heading names SpaceXAI, while his own posts describe leading recruiting at Cursor. Cursor’s acquisition announcement helps explain the different names.
demonstrates: Show how the identity check handles an apparent employer mismatch. It should explain the relationship or flag uncertainty, rather than guess that he changed jobs.

name: Don Fogarty
evidence: Make sure the research belongs to the right Don
detail: The Attio talent leader uses the LinkedIn handle /donaldfogarty. A different Don Fogarty, associated with Tango, uses /donfogarty. Searching by name alone can mix them up.
demonstrates: Show the identity confirmation step and check the company and profile before continuing. The supplied profile link helps distinguish the two people.

name: Robert Galas
evidence: Enough context to explore, with important gaps
detail: Prior research found his role and Shapr3D’s published interview process, but no clear recent hiring-expansion announcement. The careers page returned placeholder text instead of a reliable list of openings.
demonstrates: Show a restrained draft based on what the sources do establish. It should avoid inventing hiring growth, a vacancy count or problems in the team’s process.

name: Doug Parker
evidence: This team deliberately takes time to evaluate candidates
detail: Doug’s LinkedIn career details are limited, but his article on Linear’s website explains its hiring process: paid work trials, independent feedback and an emphasis on quality over speed.
demonstrates: Show research going beyond LinkedIn and a draft that respects the team’s priorities. Coordination or feedback may be worth discussing; faster decisions should not be assumed to be the goal.
